text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) might suspend all lending to Bulgaria if it fails to set up a currency board to restore confidence in the national currency, the lev, and halt inflation, an IMF official told Bulgarian government and parliamentary officials.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved a Referendum Law.
-- The parliament's agriculture committee tentatively approved a grain trade draft bill, setting grain purchase prices in foreign currency.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit overshot the 1996 target by 9.0 percent, rising to 88 billion levs at the end of October.
-- Bulgaria's opposition parties will take steps to trigger early parliamentary elections, opposition Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov said.

-- Austria-based European Privatisation and Investment Company will acquire a 1.18 billion levs stake in Bulgaria's private First Investment Bank (FIB), including 480 million levs in voting shares and 700 million in non-voting ones under a decisison by a FIB shareholders' meeting.

-- Authorities at Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Bourgas blocked iron ore and coal deliveries to Bulgaria's biggest steel works Kremikovtsi over its 292 million levs debt in shipment fees to the port, a port official said.

-- All cabinet ministers have submitted their resignations to the prime minister Zhan Videnov on Tuesday in a bid to avoid unwelcome developments ahead of a planned meeting of the Supreme Council of the ruling Socialist party on November 11, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
The meeting is expected to decide whether to vote confidence in Videnov, who is also a party chairman.
-- The central bank (BNB) approved the sale of a stake in the state owned Expressbank to the Italian Banca Agricola Mantovana. The BNB did not say how large the stake was.
-- Bulgaria stands to receive some 240 million Ecus under the European Union's PHARE programme by 1999 to support its voucher privatisation programme and private businesses, Balkan news agency said.

-- France Telecom is interested in buying a stake in the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC), a France Telecom official said after talks with the Post and Telecommunication Committee's chairman Lyubomir Kolarov. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
